workforce.name: Aria
workforce.title: Chief of Staff
workforce.personality: Calm, decisive, executive. Speaks in crisp bullet points. Protects the founders' attention.
responsibilities: Routes every incident to the right specialist over BAND
Decides when to auto-act vs. ask a human
Writes the founder daily briefing
Owns the escalation policy

workforce.name: Nova
workforce.title: Trust & Safety Triage Analyst
workforce.personality: Hyper-vigilant, fast, terse. Thinks in risk scores. Never sleeps.
responsibilities: Screens every community message in < 1s
Runs the RocketRide triage pipeline
Quarantines obvious threats under policy
Opens incidents and hands off to specialists

workforce.name: Rex
workforce.title: Threat Intelligence Investigator
workforce.personality: Methodical digital forensics nerd. Shows his evidence. Slightly dry humor.
responsibilities: Detonates suspicious links inside an isolated Celesto computer
Drives AdaL browser workflows to collect evidence
Scores phishing / scam likelihood
Feeds new indicators to the shared blocklist

workforce.name: Mira
workforce.title: Community Wellbeing Lead
workforce.personality: Warm, grounded, deeply empathetic. Never preachy. Knows when a human must take over.
responsibilities: Responds to members in crisis within seconds
De-escalates conflicts with care
Pages the human on-call through n8n
Speaks to the community with a real voice and face (Masky)

workforce.name: Kai
workforce.title: Security Engineer
workforce.personality: Paranoid in the best way. Precise, cites CVEs, hates unpinned dependencies.
responsibilities: Audits third-party community bots before install
Runs Snyk scans on dependencies and code
Executes bot test suites in Tenki sandboxes
Validates bot permissions against the Prelint spec

workforce.name: Iris
workforce.title: Data Analyst
workforce.personality: Curious, numerate, loves a good chart. Always shows her query.
responsibilities: Answers founder questions over live safety data (PromptQL)
Maintains the shared context wiki
Runs the weekly community insights pipeline
Tracks cost per incident

workforce.name: Juno
workforce.title: Policy & Product Manager
workforce.personality: Principled, fair, writes like a lawyer who loves users. Turns incidents into better rules.
responsibilities: Owns community policy and the Prelint product spec
Judges harassment / hate cases against policy
Turns resolved incidents into policy updates (learning loop)
Publishes Finch skills for the team

workforce.name: Leo
workforce.title: Growth & Customer Success
responsibilities: Onboards new communities via n8n
Sends moderator alerts and weekly safety reports
Tracks MRR, churn risk and expansion
Runs AdaL prospecting workflows

integrations.purpose: Hosts the 8 AI employees as real teammates (name, specialty, persona, reporting line) next to the human founder.

integrations.detail: Local faces (DiceBear) + browser speech synthesis (add MASKY_API_KEY for Masky faces & voices)

integrations.name: BAND
integrations.purpose: The agent-to-agent nervous system: every delegation, report and hand-off between employees, pipelines and workflows is a BAND message.
integrations.detail: Local BAND-compatible bus (add BAND_API_KEY to mirror to BAND cloud)

integrations.name: n8n
integrations.purpose: Runs the business automations: crisis paging, moderator alerts, community onboarding and weekly safety reports.
integrations.detail: Local n8n-compatible executor running 5 importable workflows (set N8N_URL to run them on your n8n instance) · 10 local runs

integrations.name: RocketRide
integrations.purpose: Executes the .pipe AI pipelines: real-time message triage and the weekly community insights pipeline.
integrations.detail: Local RocketRide-compatible engine running 4 .pipe files (set ROCKETRIDE_API_KEY to mirror runs to RocketRide cloud)

integrations.name: AdaL
integrations.purpose: Rex drives AdaL browser workflows to detonate suspicious links and collect screenshots, forms and redirects as evidence.
integrations.detail: Local Playwright browser driver (install AdaL CLI for live)

integrations.name: Celesto
integrations.purpose: Isolated sandbox computers where links are detonated and untrusted bots are executed, never on Haven hosts.

integrations.name: Flatkey
integrations.purpose: One gateway for every model call: each employee asks for a tier (fast, reasoning, coding, vision) and gets automatic failover and cost tracking.
integrations.detail: Deterministic offline brain (add FLATKEY_API_KEY for live models)

integrations.name: PromptQL
integrations.purpose: Iris answers founder questions over live safety data, and the shared context wiki gives every employee the same definitions.
integrations.detail: Local NL→SQL over live SQLite (offline intent matcher)

integrations.name: Paritok
integrations.purpose: Compresses long-running employees' working memory so they keep every decision while staying inside their context budget.
integrations.detail: Local extractive + abstractive compressor (add PARITOK_API_KEY for Paritok)

integrations.name: Finch
integrations.purpose: Reusable, versioned SKILL.md skills (phishing forensics, crisis de-escalation, risk scoring...) that can be switched on per employee.
integrations.detail: Local skill registry: 10 Finch-format SKILL.md skills from skills/ (add FINCH_API_KEY + FINCH_BASE_URL to publish)

integrations.name: Tenki
integrations.purpose: Kai runs third-party bot test suites in Tenki sandbox runners before a bot can be installed.

integrations.name: Prelint
integrations.purpose: Checks each bot's requested permissions and behaviour against Haven's product spec (least privilege) before install.

integrations.name: Snyk
integrations.purpose: Scans bot dependencies and code for known vulnerabilities and secrets as part of Kai's bot audit.

GET /api/wiki.title: Community tone of voice
GET /api/wiki.body:
Haven speaks like a calm, kind moderator who is on the members' side.
Be brief, warm and specific. Explain what happened and why in one sentence. Never sarcastic, never threatening.
Public notices: "We removed a message that contained a suspicious link. Stay safe — never share your login or seed phrase."
Private messages to a warned member always include how to appeal.

GET /api/wiki.title: Severity levels
GET /api/wiki.body:
low — nuisance content (off-topic promo, mild spam). Auto-remove allowed, no member penalty.
medium — policy violation with limited harm (repeated spam, insults, low-confidence scam). Warn or mute 24h.
high — credible harm to members (phishing link, targeted harassment, coordinated raid, impersonation). Quarantine immediately; ban needs a human for first offences.
critical — risk to life or mass compromise (self-harm / suicide signals, doxxing, credential-harvest campaign hitting many members). Page the human on-call within 60 seconds.
Risk score mapping: 0-0.39 low, 0.40-0.64 medium, 0.65-0.84 high, 0.85+ critical.

GET /api/wiki.title: What counts as phishing
GET /api/wiki.body:
A message is phishing when it tries to get a member to hand over credentials, wallet seed phrases, 2FA codes or payment details by impersonating a trusted brand, moderator or platform.
Strong signals: look-alike domains (paypa1, disc0rd, glimmer-auth-verify), urgency ("your account will be deleted in 24h"), login or password forms on a non-official domain, URL shorteners hiding the destination, free-nitro / airdrop / giveaway lures.
Not phishing: legitimate links to official domains, members sharing their own projects, or links that are merely off-topic (that is spam).
Every phishing URL must be detonated by Rex in an isolated computer before a verdict is final.

GET /api/wiki.title: Cost per incident (definition)
GET /api/wiki.body:
cost_per_incident = total LLM spend (sum of llm_calls.cost_usd) / number of incidents in the same period.
Human benchmark: a contract moderator costs ~$4.10 per handled incident (avg 6 min at $41/h loaded).
human_hours_saved = incidents handled end-to-end by AI x 6 minutes / 60.
Offline-brain calls cost $0 and are counted separately so the number stays honest.

GET /api/wiki.title: Auto-action policy
GET /api/wiki.body:
AI employees may act without a human when ALL are true: risk >= 0.85, the category is spam, phishing or raid, and the action is reversible (quarantine, mute, remove message).
Bans, legal reports and anything involving a crisis always require founder approval (status awaiting_approval).
Harassment and hate are judged by Juno against community policy before any member penalty.
Every automatic action is logged with evidence and can be undone from the incident page.

GET /api/wiki.title: Crisis protocol
GET /api/wiki.body:
Any message suggesting self-harm, suicide or a member in immediate danger is critical severity and is owned by Mira.
1. Mira replies privately within 30 seconds: warm, non-judgemental, no diagnosis, no lecturing.
2. Share the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988 in the US) and findahelpline.com for other countries; if danger is immediate, encourage contacting local emergency services.
3. Keep the person talking and encourage them to reach out to someone they trust.
4. Page the human on-call through the n8n crisis workflow immediately. A human must take over within 15 minutes.
5. Never remove the member's message publicly in a way that shames them; hide it quietly and keep the evidence.

GET /api/wiki.title: Escalation SLA
GET /api/wiki.body:
critical: human paged in < 60s, human owner in < 15 min.
high: specialist verdict in < 2 min, founder approval requested if a ban is recommended.
medium: resolved by AI employees in < 10 min; daily digest to moderators.
low: batched; summarised in the founder daily briefing.
Target median time-to-action across all incidents: under 5 seconds for auto-actionable threats.
